label: first copy-phase input (outputting orig token 1) in long sequences, boosted by m in the original
explanation: Fires only at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx == 1: input is orig token 0 fed back, output is orig token 1). Nothing fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step, or at any later copy step (9 stray activations at recall_idx 2). recall_idx==1 alone gives 99.95% mass recall but only 9% precision. Firing rate and mass rise steeply with L: L<=4 never, L=5 0.1%, L=6 1.6% of mass, L=7 11%, L=8 31%, L=9 57%. (recall_idx==1)&(L>=7) keeps 98% of mass at 17% precision. Within those steps the strongest content signal is the token m appearing in the original sequence, especially at positions 1-3. out_tok=m and next_out=m have the highest lift (7.5x and 9x), and nearly all top examples have m at orig 1-2. Adding in_orig(m) raises precision to 44% and keeps 73% of mass. Tokens 1, x, z and 3 also lift it more weakly, and more digits also raise the rate. The token dependence looks graded, like a weighted sum, rather than a clean boolean, so precision stays incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=<DEL> (+5.65), recall_idx=1 (+5.65), orig3=m (+4.67), orig1=m (+4.45), orig4=m (+3.98), orig2=m (+3.06). Lower it: orig5=- (-3.96), in_first=1 (-3.43), orig6=- (-3.25), orig8=- (-3.09).
